title: Cell configuration with lexostatus definitions v0.3.0
description: The lexostatuses a cell offers and how each is reduced from the cell's own chronicle (RFC-022 sec. 4.1, provisional there). reduction uses filter and, where needed, pick to choose a gram, and uses derivations to derive the parameters of an article: a derivation on the chosen gram (field, year_of, period_of, filled, equals, table, moment), or a derivation over the grams that pass its own filter (exists, sum, pick with field, year_of, period_of or contains). With group_by: root (and, where needed, without) the lexostatus is a list with one row per root. extra_fields supplies values that are not parameters and do not go to the engine.

law.description: Additions to the lexostatuses that the law reads in this cell (produces.extensions.chronolex.reads of an article; the lexostatus is named after the article). Only extra fields: what the cell passes along as input for a later source, not a parameter. The parameters are in the law.

extra_fields.description: Values that are not parameters, such as an input for a synthesis source. They are kept separately in the lexostatus and never go to the engine.

field_path.description: Path to a field under the gram's fields, with dots between the levels.

name.description: as_of and known_at are the reference point of a query (GET lexostatus), not inputs.

group_by.description: Turns the lexostatus into a list: one row per root (the gram without a reference that the others lead to via refers_to, such as the application). A root counts if at least one of its grams passes the filter; pick and the derivations then work per root, over its grams. A list is for the consumer and never goes to the engine; the derivations are then columns, not parameters.

without.description: Only with group_by: a root stays in the list only if none of its grams passes this filter, for example without a gram of a given stage.

pick.description: Which gram counts if there are several: latest is the gram with the latest effective_at, and with equal effective_at the latest recorded_at (a correction is a new gram). Without pick, no gram is chosen, and every derivation can only work over a set of grams.

derivations.description: Per parameter of an article under the legal_basis of the event or of the derivation itself: how it follows from the gram. May be empty if extra_fields does supply something: a lexostatus that only supplies columns for a per-row synthesis supplies no parameter.

extra_fields.description: Values that are not parameters, such as an input for a synthesis source. They are kept separately in the lexostatus and never go to the engine.

oneOf.description: The value of the field. Empty or absent: the parameter is omitted.

legal_basis.description: What this derivation rests on: the article that asks for the fact, or the article that carries the reading (such as the register the cell keeps: no gram means no). The name of a parameter derivation is a parameter of an article from the event's legal_basis or from this legal_basis. On startup: every article is loaded and the paragraph (lid) exists.

oneOf.description: The period in which a date field (YYYY-MM-DD) of the chosen gram falls, as the first day of that period (YYYY-MM-DD): a month, a quarter or a year. This makes a window a date the engine can read. No date: the parameter is omitted.

period.description: The period: year, quarter or month. Without it, the runtime takes, on startup, the temporal.period_type (year, month) of the parameter named after the derivation from the legal_basis (RFC-001): the regulation then says which period it is.

filter.description: Equality on the gram. The keys id, root, name, type, subtype, stage, recording_actor, chronicle, legal_character, decision_type, regulation and competent_authority are fields of the gram itself (root from the cell's index), and refers_to.<name> is the id the gram refers to under that name; any other key is a field path under fields. A value $<input> comes from the lexostatus inputs. The fixed values of name, type and subtype identify the event or events.

legal_basis.description: <regulation-$id>#<article-number>, optionally with ' lid <n>', as for an event (stream.json).
